PullRequest.Title: telemetry: log experiment triggers for triggered scorecards
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Adds a shared `experimentTrigger` telemetry event so that ExP triggered scorecards can be limited to users who reached the moment where an experiment's control and treatment behavior diverge. Without a trigger, assigned users whom an experiment never affects dilute its scorecard.

- `logExperimentTrigger` / `logSettingExperimentTrigger` (`src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/experimentTrigger.ts`) log `experimentTrigger { treatmentName }` at most once per window or process for each treatment. `treatmentName` is the ExP variable: `config.<setting id>` for experiment-controlled settings (via the new `getConfigurationExperimentName`, now also used by the configuration service), or the assignment-service treatment name.
- Each trigger is logged where the behavior is decided, under a condition that is computed identically in every experiment arm. Where only the treatment renders UI, the condition is evaluated as if it were enabled.

| Experiment | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `sessions.list.groupExternalSessions` | An external session that isn't pinned, done, or in a custom group is listed |
| `sessions.list.showUnreadInCollapsedSections` | A collapsed section header (any header, for screen-reader users) contains a session that needs input, is unread, or has a PR |
| `sessions.list.showArchivedByDefault` | No Done filter is chosen yet, and done content is listed, the Filter Sessions dropdown opens, or a session's context menu opens |
| `sessions.markAsDoneConfetti` | Mark as Done is clicked, except with reduced motion |
| `chat.agentSessions.archiveNudge.enabled` | The viewed session is idle with all its PRs merged, even if the nudge is off or dismissed |
| `chatSessionArchiveNudgeTitle` / `…Icon` | The nudge renders |
| `chat.experimental.openInAgentsWindow.transferDraft` | The Agents window opens from a new chat draft with content |
| `chat.agentsParallelWorkBanner.enabled` | The invitation would show, or would replace the empty-workspace handoff tip |
| `chatAgentsParallelWorkBannerTitle` / `…Description` | The invitation is shown |
| `chat.agentsHandoffTip.delaySeconds` | The handoff countdown starts |
| `chatAgentsHandoffTipTitle` / `…Description` | The tip is shown |
| `chat.agentHost.experimental.autoAttachPullRequests` | The agent host looks up a PR on a feature branch, or with PRs that restricted mode would drop; held until the assignment context arrives |

There is intentionally no trigger for `chat.agentMerge.enabled`, which changes agent tools and commands before any single visible moment, or for onboarding experiments, whose assignment context is already filtered out of telemetry until the tour would show.

Also adds an `experiments` skill that covers experiment-controlled settings, assignment-service treatments, and when and where to fire trigger events.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Archive nudge:** until a window has reported its trigger, eligibility and PR merged state are resolved even when the nudge is disabled or dismissed. Afterwards, disabled or dismissed nudges release their PR models again.
- **Draft handoff:** the chat widget is resolved before the transfer setting is checked.
- **New view items:** `SessionArchiveActionViewItem` for the Mark as Done button, and a Filter Sessions dropdown view item that reports when it opens.
- Experiments should start a new iteration once this ships, because earlier exposures have no trigger events.

## Validation

- Type check, ESLint, and layer checks report no new errors for the changed files.
- Unit tests for sessions, workbench chat, onboarding, telemetry, configuration, and agent host: 24,214 passing. New tests cover each trigger in every experiment arm.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after gate and the full call path to concrete GitHub GET requests are explicit. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often users leave a disabled/dismissed eligible session with open PRs selected and how many PRs/reviews it contains; this affects severity, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST requests and retained polling/model references
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For the currently viewed eligible session, work scales with its distinct associated PRs: each PR starts with at least two GETs (PR details and paginated reviews) and repeats them every 60 seconds; review lists over 100 entries add further page requests. The polling continues while that chat view remains active until a session's PRs are all merged and the one-time trigger is emitted.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary recurring network traffic, API-rate-limit consumption, and background CPU/allocation for users who disabled or already dismissed the feature.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The old gate returned from `eligibleSession` whenever the nudge setting was disabled or the current session was dismissed, so `models` never acquired PR model references, called `refresh()`, or started polling for that nudge.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new condition applies the disabled/dismissed gate only after `experimentTriggerPending` becomes false. On a disabled or dismissed nudge with an open PR, pending remains true, so the derived `models` path creates references, refreshes every PR immediately, and keeps their one-minute pollers alive despite no UI being shown.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `!this._nudgeService.experimentTriggerPending.read(reader) &&` prefix on line 301 bypasses the pre-existing `!enabled || isDismissed` early return until a merged-PR trigger is observed. This directly activates the unchanged model refresh/polling block for states that previously never reached it.
Findings.Title: Keep disabled and dismissed nudges out of PR polling
Findings.Impact: Opening a completed session with one or more open PRs now generates GitHub requests indefinitely even when `chat.agentSessions.archiveNudge.enabled` is false or that session's nudge was dismissed. A session with N PRs causes at least 2N immediate requests and roughly 2N requests per minute while open, potentially more for paginated reviews.
Findings.Evidence: `eligibleSession` now permits disabled/dismissed sessions while the trigger is pending (changed line 301). Its consumer at lines 311-317 maps every associated PR to `createPullRequestModelReference`, calls `model.refresh()`, and calls `model.startPolling()`. `GitHubPullRequestModel.refresh()` issues `getPullRequest` and `getReviews` concurrently, while `startPolling()` schedules another refresh every 60,000 ms. The new test explicitly changes the disabled case from expecting no requests to expecting a PR request, corroborating that this boundary work is intentional and diff-introduced.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the disabled/dismissed gate for the polling model. Derive the trigger from already-available session/PR summary state if possible, or perform a bounded one-shot status lookup only when needed; do not start recurring full PR-and-reviews polling solely to emit telemetry.

Scenarios.Scenario: View an inactive completed session whose associated GitHub pull requests are not all merged while the archive nudge is disabled or dismissed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The visible primary chat view constructs `SessionArchiveNudge`; its reactive state must resolve PR models before it can determine whether a trigger would fire. The nudge itself remains hidden, so this network work is unnecessary for user-visible progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionArchiveNudge.ts:301 and models block at 311-317, transitively GitHubPullRequestModel._refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub REST GET for PR details and one or more pages of reviews, immediately and every 60 seconds
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least 2 requests per distinct PR initially and per polling cycle; more when reviews exceed 100 entries. Shared model refreshes coalesce concurrent callers for the same PR but distinct PRs fan out independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled or dismissed state returned before PR extraction/model creation, resulting in zero nudge-owned GitHub requests and no polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required by the changed trigger derivation even though disabled/dismissed UI cannot render; repeats off the visible critical path while the chat remains selected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct artifact/session-owned PRs on the currently viewed session, plus review pagination for each PR, multiplied by minutes the eligible chat remains open before any qualifying merged state emits the process-wide trigger.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All distinct PR models are created in one array map; `void model.refresh()` starts their refreshes without a shared limiter. Each model concurrently requests PR details and reviews, while review pagination is sequential per PR. Independent one-minute schedulers can align into repeated bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR reference sharing and ETags bound duplicate payload/work but do not negative-cache the open/unmerged condition or stop periodic calls; models and pollers are released when eligibility ends, the view is disposed, or a merged session fires the global trigger.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the diff gate, reactive consumer, model refresh implementation, two concrete REST endpoints, and 60-second scheduler are directly traced; the updated test explicitly expects a request while disabled.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of completed sessions with multiple open PRs and dwell time is unknown, but stable defaults the setting to false, making the trigger-pending control path realistic. Exact API latency and rate-limit impact vary by account and repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity regression: the diff introduces recurring GitHub fan-out for users for whom the feature is disabled or already dismissed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update the Sessions list, collapse section headers, or open its filter/context menus
Scenarios.CriticalPath: List updates synchronously filter/group sessions and render visible headers; new trigger checks run inline before tree update or during header autoruns. Telemetry emission occurs at most once per treatment and does not gate rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per treatment per window/process after WeakMap/Set deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A small synchronous call occurs when the trigger first matches; subsequent matches do not emit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of sessions and chats in the list, number of rendered section/group headers, and frequency of existing list updates. Header session arrays partition/group the displayed collection; default-archive detection scans chats until a match.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread computation; no subprocess, filesystem, database, or network fan-out. Existing animation-frame scheduling coalesces active-session updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-telemetry-service treatment Set is positive-only and bounded by the finite set of treatment names reached in that window; no unbounded user-derived keys. No external data cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the scans and one-shot event exist; low that their incremental CPU is material relative to the pre-existing update pipeline.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session/chat collections can be large, but added scans are linear and comparable to existing multiple full-list passes; no concrete evidence establishes user-visible jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: bounded telemetry and linear in-memory checks do not establish a concrete performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent host reconciles or automatically associates pull requests after session restore, turn completion, or branch changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Per-session keyed sequencers serialize association work. Depending on mode and cached resolution state, the existing path may call Octokit and `git rev-parse`; the new trigger predicate runs before the mode branch but does not invoke those boundaries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Find a pull request by head branch and optionally by head SHA via Octokit
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one branch lookup and, on miss with a working directory, one SHA lookup per uncached queued association; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same association mode and lookup conditions invoked these calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed for association completion in the same scenarios as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve checkout HEAD with git `rev-parse` after a branch lookup miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per unresolved association attempt with a working directory; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical fallback existed before the trigger changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes the fallback SHA network lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit auto-attach experiment trigger telemetry after assignment context arrives
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per process for the treatment; pending state coalesces any earlier qualifying lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous telemetry invocation does not await and does not delay association.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of session/folder lookup triggers, associated/artifact PR URLs in metadata, and distinct session keys. New `wouldRestrictPullRequests` scans small URL collections per queued lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized per session/folder key by `SequencerByKey`; different keys may run concurrently as before. The diff does not change limiter or queue behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing restricted-resolution cache and keyed sequencing remain intact. The new pending boolean coalesces pre-context triggers, and the telemetry Set deduplicates later calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call conditions and serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Metadata URL arrays may vary, but they are session-associated PR collections; the added scan/allocation is bounded and not tied to a new boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: expensive GitHub/git boundaries retain their pre-diff cardinality and scheduling; additions are bounded metadata scans and one telemetry event.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents Window from a draft, evaluate the handoff tip, or update the parallel-work invitation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening resolves the relevant chat widget before checking transfer configuration, but draft serialization still occurs only when transfer is enabled/forced. Tip/banner updates synchronously evaluate model/widgets; telemetry does not await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize draft text and attachments for handoff
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per explicit open action only when transfer is enabled or forced; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Serialization had the same enabled/forced gating.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed before opening the Agents Window only for transferred drafts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit transfer, delay, banner, title, and description experiment telemetry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per treatment per window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous calls are bounded and do not await network completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat widgets/recent widgets and update events from focus, visibility, sessions, context keys, configuration, and assignment copy. The disabled parallel-work arm may perform a second widget-owner scan until the one-time trigger logs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer/workbench event handling; existing timers defer handoff-tip display. No new parallel subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are introduced by the changed predicates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The helper's per-service Set coalesces recurring `_update` events. Widget/model lookup is warm in-memory state; no negative-cache issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for changed scans and unchanged serialization gate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously registered widgets is normally small; no evidence shows the occasional second scan causes measurable input/rendering latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: additional work is bounded in-memory evaluation and once-only telemetry, with no changed expensive-boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click Mark as Done or render/archive through the archive-nudge UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Click handlers synchronously check reduced-motion state and emit the one-time setting trigger before the existing action/archive flow. Copy triggers emit when the nudge widget is constructed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per treatment per window regardless of click/widget count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous invocation before existing click behavior; no blocking await.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of clicks and widget instances, but emitted events are capped once per treatment per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency; existing archive command remains awaited as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm path is a Set membership check. Treatment names are static and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry implementation overhead varies, but cardinality is strictly bounded and payloads are tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no realistic scaling or retained-resource mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve experiment-controlled configuration defaults during workbench startup/refetch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration contribution awaits assignment-service treatment resolution as before. The refactor computes the same treatment name through a shared helper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing lookup per experiment-controlled property per refresh; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Used the identical treatment name expression inline before the helper extraction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered experiment-controlled settings; unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Assignment requests retain their prior concurrency and aggregation behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No behavior change; helper extraction preserves keys and invalidation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: semantic helper extraction does not change work or boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and traced UI, telemetry, agent-host, configuration, and GitHub boundaries. Submitted one medium-severity boundary-fanout finding: disabled/dismissed archive nudges now create and poll GitHub PR models, causing at least two recurring requests per associated PR every minute. All other additions are bounded once-per-treatment telemetry or small in-memory scans, and existing subprocess/network/serialization boundaries retain their prior cardinality.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
